blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum bachon! Aaj hum Unit 10 shuru kar rahe hain: Solution of Trigonometric Equations. Pichhli unit mein aap ne inverse trigonometric functions parhe, jahan value di hoti thi aur sirf ek angle nikalna hota tha, aur woh bhi ek khaas range ke andar. Is unit mein sawal thora bara hai: woh saare angles dhoondne hain jo kisi equation ko sach (true) bana dein. Aur aap dekhenge ke aise angles ek do nahin, balke be-shumaar (infinitely many) hote hain, kyunke trigonometric functions ghoomte pahiye ki tarah baar baar wahi values dohrate rehte hain.
Introduction

Kitab ka introduction yeh kehta hai: trigonometric equations mein \(\sin\theta\), \(\cos\theta\) aur \(\tan\theta\) jaise functions hote hain, aur inhein solve kar ke woh angle (ya angles) dhoondte hain jo di gayi shart (condition) poori karein. Is unit mein hum aisi equations ko trigonometric functions ki periodic (baar baar dohrane wali), even/odd aur translation (khisakne) wali properties se solve karenge. Maslan \(\sin\theta = k\), \(\cos\theta = k\) ya \(\tan\theta = k\) jaisi equations in functions ki periodicity dekh kar hal hoti hain. Phir hum graphical tareeqe dekhenge, jaise \(\sin\theta = \frac{\theta}{2}\), \(\cos\theta = \theta\) ya \(\tan\theta = 2\theta\) ko kisi khaas interval mein graph se solve karna. General solution mein periodicity ko istemaal kar ke \(\theta\) ki tamam mumkin values likhi jati hain. Aakhir mein inverse trigonometric functions ko engineering aur architecture ke asal masail par lagayenge: unchaai (height) nikalna, angle of elevation aur depression nikalna, aur durust scale models banana.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Shuru karne se pehle yeh chaar cheezein taaza kar lein, poori unit inhi par chalti hai:
1. Radian: \(\pi\) radian \(= 180^{\circ}\). Is liye \(\frac{\pi}{6} = 30^{\circ}\), \(\frac{\pi}{4} = 45^{\circ}\), \(\frac{\pi}{3} = 60^{\circ}\), \(\frac{\pi}{2} = 90^{\circ}\). Is unit ke saare jawab radian mein hain.
2. Standard angles par \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\tan\) ki values (neeche table hai). Yeh zabani yaad honi chahiye, jaise pahaare (tables) yaad hote hain.
3. Chaar quadrants mein kaun sa ratio positive hai (aage doosra table hai).
4. Periods: \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\csc\), \(\sec\) har \(2\pi\) ke baad dohrate hain; \(\tan\) aur \(\cot\) har \(\pi\) ke baad.

Is section ka naqsha yeh hai: pehle samjhenge ke trigonometric equation kise kehte hain aur solution, principal solution aur general solution mein kya farq hai. Phir kitab ki misaal \(\cos x = \frac{1}{2}\) se poora tareeqa seekhenge. Us ke baad teen examples: pehla seedha basic equation, doosre mein square root aur do cases, aur teesre mein squaring aur extraneous roots ka masla. Har example ke baad khud se sochne wale sawal hain; unhein chhoriye mat, wahi aap ki asal mashq hai.

blocks.caption: Hamari taraf se madad: standard angles par values, jo is unit ke taqreeban har sawal mein lagti hain

blocks.text: Trigonometric equation kya hai?

Kitab kehti hai: trigonometric equation woh equation hai jis mein ek ya zyada trigonometric functions (sine, cosine, tangent waghera) ya un ke inverse aate hon. Maslan yeh sab trigonometric equations hain:
\[\sin x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[2\cos^{2}\theta - 5\cos\theta + 1 = 0\]
\[2\tan^{-1}x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
\[\sqrt{3}\cot x - \sec x - 1 = 0\]
In mein unknown cheez angle hai (\(x\) ya \(\theta\)), number nahin. Yahi farq inhein aam algebraic equations se alag karta hai.

Angle ki woh unknown value jo di gayi trigonometric equation ko poora (satisfy) kare, us equation ka solution kehlati hai. Jo solutions interval \([0, 2\pi]\) ke andar hon, unhein principal solutions kehte hain. Trigonometric functions periodic hain, is liye aisi equations ke be-shumaar solutions hote hain. Jab ek period ke andar solution mil jaye, to us mein period ke multiples jama ya minus karne se tamam mumkin solutions mil jate hain; inhein general solution kehte hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein chhapa hai 'An unknown value of the angle that satisfy the given trigonometric equation'. 'Value' wahid (singular) hai, is liye sahi angrezi 'that satisfies' hai. Yeh sirf grammar ki ghalti hai; matlab mein koi farq nahin. Upar hum ne sahi matlab likh diya hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Teen lafz, teen alag cheezein, inhein gadmad mat kijiye:
Solution: koi ek angle jo dono sides barabar kar de. Maslan \(\sin x = 0\) ke liye \(x = \pi\) ek solution hai, kyunke \(\sin\pi = 0\).
Principal solutions: ek poore chakkar (\(0 \le x \le 2\pi\)) ke andar wale saare solutions.
General solution: har chakkar ke saare solutions, ek integer \(n\) ki madad se ek hi formula mein. \(\sin x = 0\) ke liye \(x = 0, \pm\pi, \pm 2\pi, \ldots\), yani \(x = n\pi\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).
Be-shumaar kyun? Ghari (clock) ki suiyon ko sochiye: suyi ek chakkar laga kar wapas 12 par aa jati hai, aur doosre chakkar mein bhi wahi jagah aati hai. Isi tarah angle mein \(2\pi\) jama karne se circle par wahi point aata hai aur sine, cosine wahi rehte hain. Is liye ek solution se poori family ban jati hai.
Kitab ki misaal: \(\cos x = \frac{1}{2}\)

Kitab yeh equation leti hai:
\[\cos x = \dfrac{1}{2}\]
Cosine positive hai, is liye \(x\) quadrant I aur IV mein hoga:
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
\[x = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\]
jahan \(x \in [0, 2\pi]\). Yani \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) aur \(\frac{5\pi}{3}\) is equation ke solutions hain aur inhein principal solutions kehte hain. \(\cos x\) ka period \(2\pi\) hai, is liye \(\cos x = \frac{1}{2}\) ke tamam solutions \(\frac{\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\) aur \(\frac{5\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\) hain, \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\). Is tarah general solution yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: x equals the set pi over 3 plus 2 n pi, union the set 5 pi over 3 plus 2 n pi

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(\frac{\pi}{3}\) aur \(\frac{5\pi}{3}\) aaye kahan se? Pehle woh acute angle \(\alpha\) dhoondte hain jis ka cosine \(\frac{1}{2}\) ho: \(\alpha = \frac{\pi}{3}\). Isay reference angle (hawala angle) kehte hain. Cosine quadrant I aur IV mein positive hai. Quadrant I mein angle khud \(\alpha\) hai; quadrant IV mein angle "poora chakkar minus \(\alpha\)", yani \(2\pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{5\pi}{3}\).
\(n \in \mathbb{Z}\) ka matlab: \(n\) koi bhi integer, \(\ldots, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, \ldots\). Maslan \(n = 1\) rakhein to \(\frac{\pi}{3} + 2\pi = \frac{7\pi}{3}\), aur waqai \(\cos\frac{7\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}\). \(n = -1\) rakhein to \(-\frac{5\pi}{3}\), woh bhi solution hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Khud sochiye: kya \(x = -\frac{\pi}{3}\) bhi \(\cos x = \frac{1}{2}\) ka solution hai? Agar hai to woh kis family mein aata hai? Jawab: haan, kyunke cosine even function hai, \(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}\). Aur \(-\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{5\pi}{3} - 2\pi\), yani yeh \(\frac{5\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\) wali family mein \(n = -1\) rakhne se milta hai. Matlab general solution ne koi jawab nahin chhora; yahi us ki khoobi hai.

blocks.caption: Hamari taraf se madad: reference angle ko har quadrant mein rakhna (saare angles \([0, 2\pi]\) mein)

blocks.text: Is table ko yaad rakhne ka aasaan nuskha: quadrant I se shuru kar ke ghari ki suiyon ke ulat (anticlockwise) chalein aur "All, Sin, Tan, Cos" yaad rakhein. Quadrant I mein sab (All) positive, II mein sirf sin (aur us ka ulta csc), III mein sirf tan (aur cot), IV mein sirf cos (aur sec). Angle banane ka qaida bhi tasweer se samajh aata hai: II mein hum \(\pi\) tak pohanchne se \(\alpha\) pehle ruk jate hain (\(\pi - \alpha\)), III mein \(\pi\) se \(\alpha\) aage nikal jate hain (\(\pi + \alpha\)), aur IV mein poore chakkar \(2\pi\) se \(\alpha\) pehle ruk jate hain (\(2\pi - \alpha\)).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Teenon examples mein yahi paanch qadam chalenge, inhein ratta nahin, samajh kar yaad kijiye:
1. Equation ko ek ya zyada basic equations (\(\sin x = k\), \(\cos x = k\), \(\tan x = k\)) mein badlein. Identities lagayein, factorise karein; \(x\) wala koi factor kabhi cancel na karein.
2. Positive value \(|k|\) se reference angle \(\alpha\) nikalein.
3. \(k\) ka sign dekh kar do quadrants chunein aur \([0, 2\pi]\) mein principal solutions likhein.
4. Period jama karein: \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\csc\), \(\sec\) ke liye \(+2n\pi\); \(\tan\), \(\cot\) ke liye \(+n\pi\).
5. Agar square kiya ho, kisi variable expression se multiply kiya ho, ya equation mein \(\tan\), \(\cot\), \(\sec\), \(\csc\) hon, to har root ko asal equation mein daal kar check karein.
Kuch values ka quadrant wala joda nahin banta, yeh seedhi yaad rakhein: \(\sin x = 0 \Rightarrow x = n\pi\); \(\cos x = 0 \Rightarrow x = \frac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\); \(\cos x = 1 \Rightarrow x = 2n\pi\); \(\cos x = -1 \Rightarrow x = \pi + 2n\pi\); \(\sin x = 1 \Rightarrow x = \frac{\pi}{2} + 2n\pi\); \(\sin x = -1 \Rightarrow x = \frac{3\pi}{2} + 2n\pi\).

blocks.title: Example 1
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\sin x = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).
Maloom karna: principal solutions (yani \([0, 2\pi]\) ke andar wale) aur general solution.
Tareeqa: yeh pehle se hi basic equation hai, \(\sin x = k\) wali shakal. Pehle positive number \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) se reference angle nikalenge, phir minus sign dekh kar quadrants chunenge, aur aakhir mein period \(2\pi\) jama kar ke saare solutions likhenge. Yeh tareeqa is liye theek hai ke sine ki har value circle par do jagah aati hai aur har chakkar ke baad dobara aati hai.

Reference angle nikalein
\[\sin\alpha = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
\[\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
Kyun: reference angle hamesha woh chhota (acute) angle hai jo positive value deta hai. Table yaad karein: \(\sin\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). Minus sign ko abhi ek taraf rakh dein, woh agle qadam mein kaam aayega.
Dhyan dein: \(\alpha = -\frac{\pi}{3}\) mat likhiye; reference angle kabhi negative nahin hota.

Quadrants chunein
Sine negative hai, is liye \(x\) teesre (III) aur chauthe (IV) quadrant mein hoga, aur reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) hai.
Kyun: sine sirf quadrant I aur II mein positive hota hai (unit circle par upar wala hissa). Negative sine ka matlab hai ke point circle ke neeche wale hisse mein hai, yani III ya IV.

Principal solutions
\[x = \pi + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\]
\[x = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\]
jahan \(x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
Kyun: quadrant III mein angle \(\pi + \alpha\) hota hai (aadha chakkar aur thora aage), aur quadrant IV mein \(2\pi - \alpha\) (poora chakkar se thora kam). Fractions jama karne ke liye \(\pi = \frac{3\pi}{3}\) aur \(2\pi = \frac{6\pi}{3}\) likha.

Saare solutions
\(\sin x\) ka period \(2\pi\) hai, is liye har principal solution mein \(2n\pi\) jama karte hain:
\[x = \dfrac{4\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\]
\[x = \dfrac{5\pi}{3} + 2n\pi,\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Kyun: \(2\pi\) ka matlab hai circle ka ek poora chakkar. Ek, do, ya kitne bhi chakkar laga kar hum wapas usi point par aa jate hain, is liye sine ki value nahin badalti. \(n\) koi bhi integer ho sakta hai, negative bhi (ulta chakkar).
Dhyan dein: kitab is line mein pehli family \(\frac{2\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\) chhapti hai; yeh chhapai ki ghalti hai. Sahi \(\frac{4\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\) hai (neeche "Kitab ki ghalti" dekhiye).

General solution
\[\left\{\dfrac{4\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{5\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Kyun: dono families ke saare members jawab hain. Union ka nishan \(\cup\) yahi kehta hai: pehle set ke saare members aur doosre set ke saare members, sab mila kar.

Tasdeeq:
\[\sin\dfrac{4\pi}{3} = -\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3} = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
\[\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{3} = -\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3} = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
Dono principal solutions equation ko poora karte hain. Lekin \(\sin\frac{2\pi}{3} = +\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) hai, yani \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) jawab nahin ho sakta; is se kitab ki ghalti bhi pakki ho gayi.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 1 mein kitab likhti hai ke \(\sin x = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) ke saare solutions \(\frac{2\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\) aur \(\frac{5\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\) hain. Pehli family ghalat chhapi hai; sahi \(\frac{4\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\) hai. Wajah: \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) quadrant II mein hai jahan sine positive hai, \(\sin\frac{2\pi}{3} = +\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). Kitab ki apni upar wali line (principal solutions) aur aakhri general solution mein \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\) hi sahi likha hai, is liye yeh sirf ek line ki chhapai ki ghalti hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Khud sochiye, phir jawab dekhiye:
(a) \(\cos x = -\frac{1}{2}\) ke principal solutions kya hain? Jawab: reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\), cosine negative to quadrant II aur III: \(x = \frac{2\pi}{3}, \frac{4\pi}{3}\).
(b) \(\tan x = 1\) ka general solution? Jawab: \(\frac{\pi}{4} + n\pi\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\). Yahan \(n\pi\) kyun, \(2n\pi\) kyun nahin? Kyunke tangent ka period \(\pi\) hai; \(\frac{5\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{4} + \pi\) khud hi isi family mein aa jata hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Hamari taraf se tangent ki misaal (kitab ki nahin): \(\tan x = -\sqrt{3}\) hal kijiye.
Reference angle: \(\tan\alpha = \sqrt{3}\) se \(\alpha = \frac{\pi}{3}\). Tangent negative hai, aur tangent sirf I aur III mein positive hota hai, is liye \(x\) quadrant II aur IV mein hoga: \(x = \pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) aur \(x = 2\pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{5\pi}{3}\).
Ab ghaur kijiye: \(\frac{5\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3} + \pi\). Tangent ka period \(\pi\) hai, is liye doosra jawab pehle hi ki family ka hissa hai. General solution: \(\left\{\frac{2\pi}{3} + n\pi\right\}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\). Agar aap \(\left\{\frac{2\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\} \cup \left\{\frac{5\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\}\) likhein to woh bhi bilkul sahi hai, sirf lamba hai.

blocks.title: Example 2
steps:
Diya gaya: \(2\sec^{2}x - \frac{8}{3} = 0\).
Maloom karna: principal solutions aur general solution.
Tareeqa: pehle \(\sec^{2}x\) ko akela karenge, phir square root lenge (do signs ke saath), phir secant ko cosine mein badlenge kyunke cosine ki standard values humein zabani yaad hain. Aakhir mein do basic equations alag alag solve karenge.

\(\sec^{2}x\) ko akela karein
\[2\sec^{2}x = \dfrac{8}{3}\]
\[\sec^{2}x = \dfrac{4}{3}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{8}{3}\) ko doosri taraf le gaye, phir dono taraf 2 se divide kiya. Kitab yeh chhota qadam chhor kar seedha \(\sec x\) par jati hai; hum ne yahan beech ka qadam likh diya hai.

Square root lein
\[\sec x = \pm\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\]
\[\sec x = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\ \text{ or }\ \sec x = -\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\]
Kyun: positive aur negative dono numbers ka square ek jaisa hota hai, jaise \(2^{2} = (-2)^{2} = 4\). Is liye square root lete waqt \(\pm\) zaroor likhna hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\pm\) bhool gaye to aadhe jawab (quadrant II aur III wale) gum ho jayenge.

Cosine mein badlein
\[\cos x = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
or
\[\cos x = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
Kyun: \(\cos x = \frac{1}{\sec x}\), aur \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) ko ulta karein to \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) milta hai. Secant ki values zabani yaad nahin hotin, cosine ki hoti hain; is liye yeh badlao kaam aasaan kar deta hai.

Jab \(\cos x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\)
Cosine positive hai, is liye \(x\) quadrant I aur IV mein hai, reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{6}\).
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\]
\[x = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{11\pi}{6}\]
jahan \(x \in [0, 2\pi]\). \(\cos x\) ka period \(2\pi\) hai, to saare solutions \(\frac{\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\) aur \(\frac{11\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).
Kyun: table se \(\cos\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). Cosine circle par daayen (right) hisse mein positive hai, yani quadrant I aur IV.

Jab \(\cos x = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\)
Cosine negative hai, is liye \(x\) quadrant II aur III mein hai, reference angle phir bhi \(\frac{\pi}{6}\).
\[x = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}\]
\[x = \pi + \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{7\pi}{6}\]
Period \(2\pi\), to saare solutions \(\frac{5\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\) aur \(\frac{7\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).
Kyun: reference angle hamesha positive value \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) se aata hai; minus sign sirf yeh batata hai ke point circle ke baayen (left) hisse mein hai, yani quadrant II ya III.

General solution
\[\left\{\dfrac{\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\right\} \cup \left\{\dfrac{5\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{7\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\right\} \cup \left\{\dfrac{11\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\right\}\]
jahan \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).
Kyun: equation dono cases mein se kisi bhi ek mein poori hoti hai, is liye chaaron families ka union jawab hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{5\pi}{6}, \frac{7\pi}{6}, \frac{11\pi}{6}\) chaaron par \(\cos^{2}x = \frac{3}{4}\) hai, is liye
\[\sec^{2}x = \dfrac{4}{3}\]
\[2 \cdot \dfrac{4}{3} - \dfrac{8}{3} = 0\]
Chaaron principal solutions equation ko poora karte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Example 2 ki chaar families ko chhota bhi likh sakte hain. Dekhiye: \(\frac{7\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{6} + \pi\) aur \(\frac{11\pi}{6} = \frac{5\pi}{6} + \pi\). Is liye general solution \(\left\{\frac{\pi}{6} + n\pi\right\} \cup \left\{\frac{5\pi}{6} + n\pi\right\}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\) bhi likha ja sakta hai. Dono shaklein sahi hain. Exam mein kitab wali chaar sets wali shakal zyada mehfooz hai, kyunke har set seedha ek quadrant se aata hai aur ghalti ka imkaan kam hai.

blocks.title: Remember!
blocks.text: Kitab ka Remember! box yeh kehta hai: kabhi kabhi trigonometric equation hal karne ke liye dono taraf square karna parta hai. Lekin square karne se extraneous roots (faltu, jhoote roots) aa sakte hain, yani aise jawab jo dekhne mein theek lagte hain magar asal equation ko poora nahin karte. Is liye har mumkin jawab ko asal equation mein wapas daal kar check karna zaroori hai, phir hi use qubool karein.

blocks.title: Example 3
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\sqrt{3}\cot x - \csc x - 1 = 0\) ...(1)
Maloom karna: principal solutions aur general solution.
Tareeqa: \(\cot x\) aur \(\csc x\) ko \(\sin x\) aur \(\cos x\) mein likhenge, fractions khatam karenge, phir square kar ke sirf \(\cos x\) wali equation banayenge. Square karne se kabhi kabhi jhoote (extraneous) roots aa jate hain, is liye har root ko wapas (1) mein daal kar check karenge. Yeh bhi yaad rakhein ke \(\cot x\) aur \(\csc x\) tabhi defined hain jab \(\sin x \ne 0\).

Sine aur cosine mein likhein
\[\sqrt{3}\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} - \dfrac{1}{\sin x} - 1 = 0\]
Kyun: \(\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) aur \(\csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x}\). Jab saari cheezein do hi ratios mein hon to kaam aasaan ho jata hai.

\(\sin x\) se multiply karein
\[\sqrt{3}\cos x - 1 - \sin x = 0\]
\[\sqrt{3}\cos x - 1 = \sin x\]
Kyun: har term ko \(\sin x\) se multiply karne se denominators khatam ho gaye. Yeh jaaiz hai kyunke jahan (1) defined hai wahan \(\sin x \ne 0\). Phir \(\sin x\) ko doosri taraf le gaye taa ke square kar sakein.

Dono taraf square karein
\[(\sqrt{3}\cos x - 1)^{2} = \sin^{2}x\]
\[3\cos^{2}x + 1 - 2\sqrt{3}\cos x\]
\[= \sin^{2}x = 1 - \cos^{2}x\]
Kyun: \((a - b)^{2} = a^{2} - 2ab + b^{2}\) lagaya. Square ke baad \(\sin^{2}x = 1 - \cos^{2}x\) likh sakte hain, aur poori equation sirf cosine ki ban jati hai, yani \(\cos x\) mein ek quadratic.

Terms ikatthe kar ke factorise karein
\[4\cos^{2}x - 2\sqrt{3}\cos x = 0\]
\[2\cos x\left(2\cos x - \sqrt{3}\right) = 0\]
\[\cos x = 0\ \text{ or }\ \cos x = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
Kyun: 1 dono taraf se cancel hua aur \(\cos^{2}x\) ek taraf aa gaya: \(3\cos^{2}x + \cos^{2}x = 4\cos^{2}x\). Product zero tab hi hota hai jab koi ek factor zero ho.
Dhyan dein: \(\cos x\) se divide (cancel) mat kariye; warna \(\cos x = 0\) wala case, aur us ke saath asal jawab \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\), gum ho jayega.

Jab \(\cos x = 0\)
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\ \text{ and }\ x = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\]
jahan \(x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
Kyun: unit circle par cosine (yani x-coordinate) sirf sab se upar aur sab se neeche wale points par zero hota hai.

\(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) ko (1) mein check karein
\[\sqrt{3}\cot\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \csc\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 1\]
\[= \sqrt{3}(0) - 1 - 1 = -2 \ne 0\]
To \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) equation ko poora nahin karta: yeh extraneous root hai.
Kyun: \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) par \(\sqrt{3}\cos x - 1 = -1\) hai magar \(\sin x = +1\). Dono ke squares barabar (1) hain lekin khud numbers barabar nahin. Yeh root square karne ki wajah se ghus aaya tha.

\(x = \frac{3\pi}{2}\) ko (1) mein check karein
\[\sqrt{3}\cot\dfrac{3\pi}{2} - \csc\dfrac{3\pi}{2} - 1\]
\[= \sqrt{3}(0) - (-1) - 1 = 0\]
To \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) asal solution hai. \(\cos x\) ka period \(2\pi\) hai, is liye general values \(\frac{3\pi}{2} + 2n\pi\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).
Kyun: \(\cot\frac{3\pi}{2} = 0\) aur \(\csc\frac{3\pi}{2} = \frac{1}{\sin(3\pi/2)} = \frac{1}{-1} = -1\). Minus minus plus ho kar \(+1\) bana, jo aakhri \(-1\) ko cancel kar deta hai.

Jab \(\cos x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\)
Cosine positive hai, is liye \(x\) quadrant I aur IV mein hai, reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{6}\).
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\]
\[x = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{11\pi}{6}\]
jahan \(x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
Kyun: \(\cos\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\); quadrant IV ka angle \(2\pi - \alpha\) hota hai.

\(x = \frac{\pi}{6}\) ko (1) mein check karein
\[\sqrt{3}\cot\dfrac{\pi}{6} - \csc\dfrac{\pi}{6} - 1\]
\[= \sqrt{3}\cdot\sqrt{3} - 2 - 1 = 3 - 3 = 0\]
To \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) asal solution hai; general values \(\frac{\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).
Kyun: \(\cot\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{\tan(\pi/6)} = \sqrt{3}\) aur \(\csc\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{\sin(\pi/6)} = 2\).

\(x = \frac{11\pi}{6}\) ko (1) mein check karein
\[\sqrt{3}\cot\dfrac{11\pi}{6} - \csc\dfrac{11\pi}{6} - 1\]
\[= \sqrt{3}(-\sqrt{3}) - (-2) - 1\]
\[= -3 + 2 - 1 = -2 \ne 0\]
To \(\frac{11\pi}{6}\) bhi extraneous root hai.
Kyun: quadrant IV mein \(\cot\) aur \(\csc\) dono negative hote hain: \(\cot\frac{11\pi}{6} = -\sqrt{3}\), \(\csc\frac{11\pi}{6} = -2\). Signs badalne se jawab zero nahin banta.

General solution
\[\left\{\dfrac{3\pi}{2} + 2n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\right\},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Kyun: sirf woh do roots rakhe jo check mein paas hue, aur har ek ke saath us ka period \(2\pi\) laga diya.

Tasdeeq:
Dono rakhe gaye roots upar (1) mein poore utre. Dono par \(\sin x \ne 0\) hai (\(\sin\frac{3\pi}{2} = -1\), \(\sin\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{2}\)), is liye \(\cot x\) aur \(\csc x\) wahan defined bhi hain.
blocks.answer: Principal solutions: \(x = \frac{\pi}{6}\) aur \(x = \frac{3\pi}{2}\) (\(\frac{\pi}{2}\) aur \(\frac{11\pi}{6}\) extraneous hain). General solution: \(\left\{\frac{3\pi}{2} + 2n\pi\right\} \cup \left\{\frac{\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\right\}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Example 3 mein square karne se faltu roots kyun aaye? Agar \(A^{2} = B^{2}\) ho, to \(A = B\) bhi ho sakta hai aur \(A = -B\) bhi. Jab hum ne \(\sqrt{3}\cos x - 1 = \sin x\) ko square kiya, to anjaane mein \(\sqrt{3}\cos x - 1 = -\sin x\) bhi saath hal ho gayi. \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) aur \(\frac{11\pi}{6}\) isi doosri equation ke roots hain (maslan \(\frac{11\pi}{6}\) par \(\sqrt{3}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - 1 = \frac{1}{2}\) jab ke \(\sin\frac{11\pi}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}\)). Misaal: \(x = 3\) ko square karein to \(x^{2} = 9\), jis ke jawab \(3\) aur \(-3\) hain; \(-3\) faltu mehmaan hai. Asal equation mein check karna hi us mehmaan ko bahar nikalta hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Khud sochiye: Example 3 mein hum ne \(\sin x\) se multiply kiya. Agar kisi root par \(\sin x = 0\) hota (maslan \(x = \pi\)), to kya woh jawab ho sakta tha? Jawab: nahin, kyunke wahan \(\cot x\) aur \(\csc x\) defined hi nahin (zero se taqseem). Is liye aisi equations mein shuru hi mein likh lein ke \(x \ne 0, \pi, 2\pi\), aur aakhir mein dekh lein ke koi jawab in mein se to nahin. Yahan koi nahin tha, is liye sirf squaring wale faltu roots hataane pare.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Hamari taraf se ek aur misaal (kitab ki nahin): \(2\sin x + 1 = 0\) hal kijiye.
Pehle basic shakal: \(\sin x = -\frac{1}{2}\). Reference angle: \(\sin\alpha = \frac{1}{2}\) se \(\alpha = \frac{\pi}{6}\). Sine negative, to quadrant III aur IV: \(x = \pi + \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{7\pi}{6}\) aur \(x = 2\pi - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{11\pi}{6}\). Period \(2\pi\), to general solution \(\left\{\frac{7\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\right\} \cup \left\{\frac{11\pi}{6} + 2n\pi\right\}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\). Tasdeeq: \(2\sin\frac{7\pi}{6} + 1 = 2\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) + 1 = 0\).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Khud sochiye: \(\sin x = 2\) ka koi solution kyun nahin? Jawab: sine ki value hamesha \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan rehti hai, is liye 2 kabhi nahin ban sakti. Isi tarah \(\cos x = -3\) ka bhi koi solution nahin. Equation hal karte waqt agar aisi value aa jaye to woh case seedha rad (reject) kar dein.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Trigonometric equation mein angle dhoonda jata hai. Principal solutions \([0, 2\pi]\) mein hote hain; general solution poore periods jama kar ke likha jata hai aur saath \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\) zaroor likhte hain.
2. Reference angle positive value se, quadrants sign se: I mein \(\alpha\), II mein \(\pi - \alpha\), III mein \(\pi + \alpha\), IV mein \(2\pi - \alpha\).
3. \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\sec\), \(\csc\) ka period \(2\pi\); \(\tan\), \(\cot\) ka period \(\pi\).
4. Square root lete waqt \(\pm\); dono cases hal karein aur general solution mein saari families ka union likhein.
5. Square karne ke baad, ya jab \(\cot\), \(\csc\), \(\tan\), \(\sec\) hon, har root asal equation mein check karein aur extraneous roots rad kar dein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Negative value se reference angle nikalna, maslan \(\sin x = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) ke liye sirf \(x = -\frac{\pi}{3}\) likh kar ruk jana. Reference angle \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) se aata hai; sign sirf quadrant batata hai.
2. Sirf ek principal solution likhna. \(\sin x = k\) ya \(\cos x = k\) (jahan \(-1 < k < 1\), \(k \ne 0\)) ke \([0, 2\pi)\) mein hamesha do solutions hote hain.
3. Square root lete waqt \(\pm\) bhool jana (Example 2 mein aadhe jawab gum ho jate).
4. \(\cos x\) jaisa factor cancel kar dena, factorise karne ki bajaye (Example 3 mein \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) gum ho jata).
5. Square karne ke baad check na karna (Example 3 mein \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) aur \(\frac{11\pi}{6}\) ghalti se jawab ban jate).
6. General solution ke saath \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\) na likhna, ya degree aur radian mila dena.
